newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks end lower on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks end lower on profit-taking.

text.p: Swiss shares ended one percent lower on Friday as profit-taking, a weaker dollar and losses in early Wall Street trade took their toll, dealers said.
Friday's drop followed a two percent rise in the leading share Swiss Market Index (SMI) Thursday.
Demand centered on electrical engineering group ABB Asea Brown Boveri, one of the few SMI stocks to post gains.
ABB rose 35 francs to 2,301 after private bank Pictet & Cie raised its target price for ABB's registered share to 2,800 francs.
The SMI ended 0.96 percent lower, or 57.3 points, at 5,864.8 and the all-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) ended down 0.80 percent or 30.28 at 3,738.09.
CS Group also attracted attention, amidst renewed rumours that the group was considering an unspecified acquisition.
CS Group declined to comment on the rumours.
The stock rose one franc to 208,50.
UBS dropped 13 francs to close at 1,647 while SBC lost 4.50 francs to close at 412.
Chemical and pharmaceuticals were under pressure. Volume leader Novartis dropped 50 francs to 2,342, while its rival Roche ended 140 francs below Thursday's close at 14,520.
Clariant declined 17 francs to end at at 1,074 and Ciba Specialty was fractionally lower, losing 0.50 francs to 142.50. Ems dropped 20 francs to 6,830.

Insurers Zurich and Swiss Re gained initially on recommendations and market views that the insurance sector would perform well. Zurich rose one franc to 614, while Swiss Re dropped 11 francs to 2,186.
Winterthur continued its upward move and rose eight francs to 1,515.
